clue.text: Rock teacher — he's a real pain

parts.note: a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill, as on Dartmoor
a mentor is a trusted adviser or teacher

explanation.surface: A rock music teacher is described as a thorough nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like music but is the craggy hilltop TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who persecutes and torments others is, colloquially, a real pain to be around.

clue.text: Will set up 19, not being heartless

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
the solution to 19 across, meaning docile or flat

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word not is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone's will is drawn up with reference to clue 19, minus a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SET to TES; 'being heartless' strips the O from NOT to leave NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document disposing of a person's estate after death.

clue.text: The tracks of birds

definitions.meaning: the metal lines that trains run along
the crake family of marsh-dwelling birds, such as the corncrake and water species

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the steel bars of a railway line and a family of secretive wading birds.

clue.text: Swiss place where many people get in awfully late

indicators.note: get in tells us one group of letters goes inside another
awfully signals that the letters of late are jumbled

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
men is a common word for people

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Switzerland lots of folk arrive dreadfully late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges LATE to ETAL; 'get in' places M and MEN inside it after the first E. The Emmental is a valley in Switzerland, famous for its cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmental is a valley in the Swiss canton of Bern, which gave its name to the holey cheese.

clue.text: He's responsible for the water supply off and on

definitions.text: He's responsible for the water supply off and on

parts.words: He's responsible for the water supply off and on
parts.note: describes a water-board official whose job is to open and close the mains valves, the 'off and on' looking like 'intermittently'

explanation.definitionFit: A turncock was a waterworks employee who opened and shut the stopcocks on water mains.

clue.text: Descriptive summary about runners-up

parts.note: re is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the runners are written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds that run rather than fly

explanation.surface: A brief summary concerns the competitors who finished second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners-up' looks like the second-placed finishers, but splits into runners (EMUS) and 'up', which reverses them to SUME.
explanation.definitionFit: A résumé is a short account summing up the main points of something.

clue.text: The old buffoon putting a worker in charge

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: An old clown puts an employee in a position of responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespearean English the word meant a clown or grotesque jester; 'the old' marks it as archaic.

clue.text: A serving man will be in trouble when slow

indicators.note: will be in tells us the first pieces sit inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado
a GI is an American serviceman, a soldier

explanation.surface: A waiter is going to get into bother when service is sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving man' looks like a waiter but is a soldier, GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical tempo marking for a slow, leisurely pace.

clue.text: Court officials find two ways to split gratuities

indicators.note: to split means the two ways are driven into the middle of the gratuities

parts.note: tips are gratuities left for service
ST is the abbreviation for street, one way
AVE is the abbreviation for avenue, the second way

explanation.surface: Legal officers discover a couple of methods to share out tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ways' means roads here, not methods.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipstaves are court officers, named after the metal-tipped staff they carried as a badge of office.

clue.text: Ring left out for an enchantress

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is dropped from the word for ring

parts.note: a circle is a ring

explanation.surface: A ring is omitted in favour of a sorceress.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey this sorceress turns Odysseus's men into swine, the archetypal enchantress.

clue.text: Seethe about someone unused to driving faster

indicators.note: about means the word for seethe goes around the learner

parts.note: to simmer is to seethe quietly with anger
L is the learner driver's plate, so a novice behind the wheel

explanation.surface: A driver fumes about a novice going quicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faster' looks like 'quicker' but means one who fasts, a dieter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dieter cutting down on food is one who fasts, a faster.

clue.text: Fish photographer?

definitions.meaning: a reddish food fish of warm seas
slang for one who takes quick pictures, with the question mark flagging the playful sense

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sea fish and, informally, a press cameraman who takes shots.

clue.text: Lighting up is a punishable offence!

definitions.text: Lighting up is a punishable offence!

parts.words: Lighting up is a punishable offence!
parts.note: reads like a no-smoking warning, but lighting up a building means setting it ablaze criminally

explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property, a lighting-up that the law punishes.

clue.text: The council having business met, time being made for this

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: being made signals that the letters of met and time are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: Council members having met on business set aside time for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being made' rearranges METTIME into MMITTEE, which follows CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A council is a body of people appointed to deliberate, which is what a committee is.

clue.text: Charm that's not way-out

definitions.meaning: to charm is to enchant or delight
the opposite of an exit is a way in

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb stressed on the second syllable it means to bewitch; as a noun it is a door or way in, the opposite of an exit.

clue.text: Clement, showing some irascibility, took the fare

parts.note: temper is a fit of irascibility, as in losing one's temper
ate means consumed food, the fare on offer

explanation.surface: Clement showed a flash of bad temper while eating the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clement' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning mild.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild and moderate, as is a temperate climate.

clue.text: Found in a very bad state

indicators.note: found in signals the letters are lurking inside the words a very bad

explanation.surface: Something is discovered in really poor condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a condition but is the verb to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare something positively.

clue.text: A home vandalised — dire scene!

indicators.note: vandalised signals that the letters of dire scene are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A house has been trashed, a dreadful sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling or home.

clue.text: Predict elevation of count yet again

indicators.note: in a down clue elevation means the word is raised, written upwards and so backwards

parts.note: to retell is to recount or narrate again

explanation.surface: Forecast the raising of a nobleman once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevation of' turns OF into FO; 'count' is not a nobleman but to recount, told again.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell is to prophesy or say beforehand what will happen.

clue.text: Point to a man of the type to be a runner

parts.note: S for south is a compass point
a printer is a man who works with type

explanation.surface: Indicate a fellow of the right character to be a racer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the type' looks like 'of the right sort', but means working with printing type.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is someone who runs short distances fast.

clue.text: Flat meat pie

indicators.note: in printing, pie is type that has been jumbled, so the letters of meat are scrambled

explanation.surface: A level meat pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' is the printers' term for jumbled type, an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and lacking excitement can be called tame or flat.

clue.text: Forms or settles

definitions.meaning: makes up or constitutes, as parts form a whole
calms down, as one settles oneself

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to make up or constitute something and to calm or settle oneself.

clue.text: Turn up in green

parts.note: vert is the heraldic term for green

explanation.surface: Appear in green.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is green in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: To invert is to turn something upside down.

clue.text: It could be a mother and father split

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a rent is a tear or split

explanation.surface: A mother and father could separate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a mother and father' looks like the definition, but 'and' is a link and 'father' gives PA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is one example of a parent; 'could be' signals the example.

clue.text: Producing such fruit presents the environmentalist with a challenge

parts.note: a green is an environmentalist or ecology campaigner
a gage is a pledge thrown down as a challenge to fight

explanation.surface: Growing these plums gives eco-campaigners a test.
explanation.walkthrough: A GAGE was a glove or token thrown down as a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a kind of plum, the fruit referred to.

clue.text: Equipment stand

definitions.meaning: an outfit or costume one is kitted out in

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means an outfit or kit; as a phrasal verb it means to rise from sitting.

clue.text: One dunderhead went ahead but accomplished nothing

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word dunder

parts.note: led means went in front

explanation.surface: A fool took the lead but achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like a fool but splits to give the head, D, of 'dunder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who idled loafed about without doing anything useful.

clue.text: Study is to be made of renal failure

indicators.note: failure signals that the letters of renal break down and rearrange

explanation.surface: Kidney failure needs to be investigated.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a subject is to acquire knowledge of it.

clue.text: A high-flier may well depend on it

definitions.text: A high-flier may well depend on it

parts.words: A high-flier may well depend on it
parts.note: a high-flier sounds like an ambitious achiever, but here is a circus acrobat swinging high above the ring

explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is the swinging bar on which aerial acrobats perform.

clue.text: Possibly ten come down and get on board

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of ten could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: rain is what comes down from the sky

explanation.surface: Perhaps ten will descend and climb aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TEN to ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a train.

clue.text: Double back to see an Irishman set about the French

indicators.note: set about means the Irishman's name is placed around the French article

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish name, short for Patrick
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Retreat to visit an Irish fellow who is attacking the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double back' looks like retreat but means fold over.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold of cloth doubled back on itself and pressed.

clue.text: To cut without hesitation shows open-mindedness

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for cut goes around the hesitation

parts.note: to lance a boil is to cut it
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Cutting straight in with no pause reveals a liberal attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: LANCE goes around ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is willingness to accept views different from one's own.
